description: This circular walk takes you across Blubberhouses Moor, a rugged expanse nestled in the heart of North Yorkshire. The route begins at the moor’s edge, where sweeping vistas reveal a tapestry of rolling hills, remote farmland, and the distinctive character of an open, windswept landscape. As you make your way along the path, the interplay of light and shadow across the heather-clad slopes and expansive boggy areas invites reflection and a deep connection with the natural beauty and historical tapestry of the region. Remnants of ancient field systems and stone boundary walls hint at centuries of agricultural heritage, adding a layer of cultural significance to this evocative setting. Blubberhouses Moor is celebrated for its resilient ecosystem, which supports a diverse array of flora and fauna well adapted to the moorland environment. The terrain is predominantly carpeted with heather, bilberry, and robust grasses, intermingled with gorse and other hardy shrubs that flourish in the exposed conditions. In spring and summer, the moor comes alive with wildflowers that punctuate the landscape with vibrant bursts of colour. The area also provides an ideal habitat for a variety of bird species, including skylarks, meadow pipits, and wheatears, while small mammals and an abundance of insects contribute to a balanced, dynamic ecosystem that is a delight for naturalists and wildlife enthusiasts alike. At the eastern end of the route you can also enjoy a waterside walk along Fewston Reservoir .
